anomalies.observed: The two interchangeable MCU footprints assign the POT and TACH nets to opposite physical pins. On U2 (ATtiny45-20P, THT) the label POT is on pin 2 and TACH on pin 3, while on U3 (ATtiny13V-10S, SMD) POT is on pin 3 and TACH on pin 2. Both symbols otherwise map pin 2 = PB4 and pin 3 = PB3, so POT ends up on PB4 for U2 but on PB3 for U3, and TACH the reverse.
anomalies.expected: Alternative THT/SMD footprints of the same device must present an identical net-to-pin mapping so that a single firmware build works whichever footprint is populated. The spec describes the board as 'an ATtiny-driven fan controller' (a single MCU), so the two footprints are meant to be interchangeable and must agree.

evidence.quote: U2 ATtiny45-20P (THT): pin 5 SDA, 6 PWM, 7 SCK, 2 POT, 3 TACH, 1 RST
U3 ATtiny13V-10S (SMD): pin 5 SDA, 6 PWM, 7 SCK, 3 POT, 2 TACH, 1 RST

anomalies.impact: Populating U2 instead of U3 (or vice-versa) swaps the potentiometer set-point input and the fan tachometer feedback input on the microcontroller. The firmware would read the wrong ADC channel for the set point and the wrong pin for RPM feedback, so closed-loop fan control would not work for one of the two build variants.

parsed.summary: The schematic is largely a coherent ATtiny fan controller (5V regulator, I2C header, pot input, high-side PMOS fan switch with NPN driver, tach/reset pull-ups, decoupling), but the two interchangeable MCU footprints U2 and U3 assign the POT and TACH nets to opposite pins, an inconsistency that breaks firmware compatibility between the THT and SMD build variants.
